svg.title: Figure 1 — LC-TEM nanoparticle analysis pipeline
svg.text: Figure 1 | End-to-end pipeline for phase analysis of liquid-cell TEM nanoparticle videos
Raw low-dose AVI → drift correction → self-supervised denoising → SAM 3 segmentation → per-frame crystallographic phase timeline
jitter but keeps the slow physical drift
Smoothed shifts applied to the RAW frames
(no cross-frame mixing yet — mask stays exact)
the centre frame is zeroed: the network cannot
see the frame it is asked to predict
the target is the NOISY centre frame
Keep the best mask with score ≥ 0.3 and
Square side = max(Δx, Δy) × 0.6, centred on
particle fills a constant fraction of the frame
validation on the real, particle-level split (1 214 images) unless noted
real + synthetic, validated on real only
Ensembling was tested and rejected — averaging the best model with the two combined-data models reaches only 95.88 %,
below the single best model with TTA. Single frames of Ih and Ih→Dh are not separable, which is why the 4-class model
loses 7 points; the transition class is recovered from temporal context instead (Stage 4, step 5).
offline — not part of per-video inference
Split by PARTICLE, 90/10 — both frames of a particle stay on one side; a
per-image split would leak particle identity into validation.
Class imbalance (Ih : FCC ≈ 11 : 1) is handled with an inverse-frequency
